Case 01 — L·AI·C
Case 01 · 2024
L·AI·C
AI concierge for 800K+ Life Time members
UX Design Strategy Conversational Design 2024

L·AI·C was already being built when I joined. Engineering had moved fast — but no one had defined what the AI should say, how it should think, or why members would use it.

I went back to the beginning. Interviewed the concierge team, mapped the most repeated questions, and designed the full conversation routing — what L·AI·C could answer, what it couldn't, and where to send users when it hit its limit.

Every dead end became a pathway. Every question became a conversion opportunity.

Case 02 — On Demand
Case 02 · 2024
On Demand
Filter, sort, and actually find a class — 800K+ Life Time members
Product Design UX Research Information Architecture 2024

On Demand had thousands of classes and no way to sort through them. The library grew faster than the way people could find anything in it — no filter, no sort, no way to narrow by duration, level, or coach.

I audited the full content catalogue, ran 20+ user sessions, and benchmarked Peloton, Apple Fitness+, and Nike Training across six dimensions. Duration surfaced as the most-requested filter by a wide margin — so the system was rebuilt around it, then expanded to nine dimensions members could actually navigate.

Category → discipline → your class. One clear path where there used to be none.

Harsh Chaudhary

Product Designer · 2026

I've always been someone who likes making things.

Digital design is where I've spent the last six years, but I've never thought of creativity as something that fits into a single box. I've worked across consumer products, branding, visual systems, websites, and strategic communications, helping teams take ideas from concept to launch. Whether I'm designing an app or shaping a brand, I enjoy making complex ideas feel simple, thoughtful, and intuitive.

Lately, a lot of that curiosity has been directed toward AI. I'm interested in how new tools are changing the way we design and build products, and I enjoy experimenting with them to understand where they genuinely improve the creative process.

Outside of work, I'm building jnpr.labs, a creative space where I explore ideas that don't always fit inside my day job. It's become a place to experiment with branding, product concepts, AI workflows, and digital products. More recently, I've started creating design reviews and video essays, breaking down products I admire to understand what makes them intuitive and sharing those insights with the design community on Instagram. I also create templates and resources to help other creatives build better work.

Outside of work, I spend a lot of my time creating. Recently I've been learning music production, which has been a fun reminder that the creative process is surprisingly similar across disciplines. Whether I'm designing a product or producing a song, I enjoy the challenge of shaping something from an idea into a finished piece. When I need to step away from the screen, you'll usually find me hiking, swimming, practicing yoga, or spending time outdoors.

Curious about what guides my work? Open the notebook on the desktop.
